title:
Comment of Evelyn Waltenbaugh in Docket(s)/Project(s) P-15423-000
Submission Date: 11/2/2026

documents.name: 152079.txt
documents.text:
Evelyn Waltenbaugh, Homer, AK.
Regarding:  DeepGreen ‘s proposal in Cook Inlet to seek a federal permit to install a tidally powered data center in the Forelands region near Nikiski.

We live on the Kenia Peninsula and are concerned about the potential impacts of the DeepGreen’s proposal. 

This is an enormous development that hasn’t been done before.  In fact, a small experimental in Scotland from 2018 to 2020 was confirmed in 2024 that they didn’t plan to pursue the project further. 

The prospect of a large underwater data center requires sound science rather than techno-hype before allowing such a center.  Our waters need to be  protected from:

*hydroacoustic noise form tidal generators need to be proven with small projects before allowing such a large scale of generators.
*water warming effects in a narrow bottleneck of Cook Inlet.  The potential to affect health or behavior of salmon plankton, or other marine life is unknown.
*waste heat that would expose seawater, strong current, and slit might be an area of concern itself.  Along with copper can be toxic to salmon

*electricity during low tides could potentially result in shortages of electricity for communities of Alaska along with higher cost of electricity (which is already very high for the Kenia Peninsula.

The communities of Cook Inlet | Tikahtnu deserve thoughtful, sustainable solutions that truly serve local needs. Rather than prioritizing massive, energy-intensive data centers, we should focus on projects that deliver reliable, renewable energy and protect the region’s salmon and ecosystems for future generations.

We do not need an energy-intensive data centers in our community.  Please do not approve DeepGreen’s proposal.
